requirement: Chart daily signups over a requested date range as a gap-free UTC series where days without signups show zero.
skeleton: daily_signups validating the range, parsing timestamps to UTC, counting ones with resample by day, and reindexing onto a UTC date_range with fill_value 0 as an int64 series named signups.
caption: Turning signup events into a complete daily series with pandas resample. daily_signups(events, start, end) raises ValueError saying start must not be after end when the range is reversed. It parses created_at with pd.to_datetime utc True, builds a Series of ones indexed by those instants, sorts it, and counts per day with resample D. It then reindexes onto pd.date_range from start to end with daily frequency, tz UTC and index name day, using fill_value 0 so days with no signups and days outside the data appear as zero, casts to int64 and names the series signups. The fixture asserts counts 1, 1, 3, 0, 0 for January 1 to 5 as int64, an index named day in UTC with the expected dates and series name signups, that an event at 23:30 at offset -02:00 on January 1 counts on January 2, and that a reversed range raises ValueError.

constraints: Timestamps are bucketed by UTC day
Every day in the range appears once
Days without events are 0 not NaN
The result is int64 named signups with index day

rationale.teaches: Resample to the target frequency, then reindex onto an explicit timezone-aware date_range with fill_value so the series has no holes.
rationale.why: resample only covers the observed span, NaN gaps break integer charts, and bucketing local offsets moves late-night signups to the wrong day.

ops.docstring: Aggregate signups into a complete daily UTC series with zero-filled gaps.

candidates.why_wrong: Days without signups become NaN and the integer cast fails.
A naive date_range cannot align with the UTC counts, so every day reads zero.
A reversed range silently returns an empty series instead of raising.
Hourly buckets make each day count only signups in its first hour.
Mixed offsets are not normalized to UTC before daily bucketing.
